subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw implement native core per-agent spend-budget enforcement, expose only a budget-capable plugin/admission API, or leave spend limits to external/provider-account controls?
rationale: The remaining work changes config/defaults, provider dispatch policy, persistent accounting state, and operator UX, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Native core admission layer
options.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets as a core pre-dispatch admission path with durable SQLite accounting, reservations/refunds, receipts, and status/doctor surfaces.

options.title: Plugin/API-first boundary
options.body: Extend hooks or plugin APIs with budget state and reservation primitives, then let a plugin or external system own policy.

options.title: External controls only
options.body: Keep OpenClaw to usage reporting and document provider accounts, external wallets, and proxies as the supported budget-control path.

recommendation.title: Native core admission layer
recommendation.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets as a core pre-dispatch admission path with durable SQLite accounting, reservations/refunds, receipts, and status/doctor surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest recent history across the current cost-reporting, config-schema, and release surfaces that would be touched by this decision.
